sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the upload library, its styling, the storage connector and the app's button.
sections.why: Standard setup for the upload tool and its popup.
sections.watch_out: Removing the style imports would leave the popup unstyled.

sections.name: ObjectUploaderProps
sections.title: Settings the parent passes in
sections.what: Lists what a parent page must supply: a file count limit, a size limit per file, a function that asks the server for an upload address, an optional completion callback, a style class and the button content.
sections.why: Lets the same upload button be reused in several places with different rules.
sections.watch_out: The address function is called once for each file, so it must return a fresh address every time.

sections.name: ObjectUploader (part 1)
sections.title: Upload controller settings
sections.what: Sets up the upload controller once: a default of one file and a 10 MB limit, direct upload to storage in one piece, and no automatic start, so the user presses start. When all uploads finish, it calls the parent's callback.
sections.why: Likely reason: one upload per file with no splitting, and the user confirms before anything starts.
sections.watch_out: The controller is created only once, so later changes to the limits, the address function or the completion callback are not used.

sections.name: ObjectUploader (part 2)
sections.title: Button and popup
sections.what: Shows the button. Pressing it opens the upload popup, and closing the popup hides it. The popup's credit line is turned off.
sections.why: Reason for hiding the credit line not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The controller is not shut down when the button leaves the page, so this is not cleaned up in the code shown.

summary: A button that opens a popup where a user picks files and uploads them straight to cloud storage using one-time addresses supplied by the server.
purpose: Lets any page offer a file upload with the same popup, without writing the upload logic each time.
why: The header says the Uppy popup handles all file management. Likely reason: one shared component so uploads look and behave the same everywhere.
how: 1. The parent page places the button and passes its settings. 2. Pressing the button opens the popup. 3. The user chooses files, and the popup checks the file count and size. 4. For each file, the parent's function asks the server for an upload address. 5. The file is sent to that address. 6. When all uploads finish, the completion callback runs so the parent can record the result.
inputs: Settings: a file count limit, a size limit, the function that gets upload addresses, an optional completion callback, and the button style and label. Also the files the user picks.
outputs: Files sent to storage and a completion callback with the result. The component saves nothing itself.
risks: The default size limit is 10 MB. A wrong upload address function makes every upload fail. Settings are fixed after the first display. The upload controller is never shut down, so it may keep files in memory.
debug: If uploads fail, check the server response that gives the upload address, then the browser network tab. If limits seem ignored, reload the page, because the controller keeps its first settings. If the completion step does not run, check that the callback was passed and that all uploads finished.
